images.caption: This figure illustrates how large language models (LLMs) struggle with salience bias and sycophancy. Panel (a) shows poor overall trap avoidance across 12 LLMs, while panel (b) demonstrates that increasing the number of numeric distractors correlates with lower trap avoidance (TAR) and higher CoT-hijacking. Panels (c) and (d) reveal that even when models detect a trap, they often still comply with it, although removing framing artifacts ("context-free") significantly improves their performance.

This figure presents a decision-making flow for choosing between driving or walking after getting a car washed. It outlines different scenarios that lead to specific recommendations, concluding with a suggested action to walk and a prompt for further reasoning.

This bar chart illustrates the liberation rate across four different language models—Claude-4.6, GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2, and DeepSeek-R1—under three distinct debiasing prompt conditions: Premise Hint, Trap Reveal, and Knowledge Probe. The results show that the effectiveness of these progressive debiasing strategies varies significantly by model, with most models achieving high liberation rates exceeding 90% in at least one condition.

This bar chart compares the Trap Avoidance Rate (TAR) across three large language models (Claude-4.6, GLM-5.1, and DS-V4-Pro) under four different prompt-level interventions: Control, Physics-Aware Priming, Forced CoT Premise-Check, and Counterfactual Warning. The results demonstrate that the Physics-Aware Priming intervention consistently yields the highest TAR across all three models, while the Control group consistently performs the lowest.
